answer.line: 360 miles in 3.6 + 2.4 = 6 hours is 60 mph. The slow leg takes longer, so it pulls the average down.

steps: Name the rule: average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds.
Time each leg: 180 / 50 = 3.6 hours out, and 180 / 75 = 2.4 hours back.
Whole trip: 360 miles in 6 hours. 360 / 6 = 60 mph.
Check it: more hours at 50 mph than at 75, so the answer sits below the midpoint of 62.5.

choices.note: No standard slip lands on 68.8. It sits above the midpoint, but the slow leg's extra hours pull the average below 62.5.
61.2 is the root of 50 x 75, the geometric mean of the speeds. Average speed is total distance over total time.
30 uses the right total time, 6 hours, but only one leg of distance, 180 miles. The trip is 360 miles.
62.5 averages 50 and 75 as if the driver spent equal time at each. The 50 mph leg takes longer, so it counts more.

lockIt: Average speed is total distance over total time. Equal distances give the slower speed more weight.
